problem: SLAM-based semantic-mapping ObjectNav pipelines rely on a pretrained detector (e.g. Mask R-CNN) to label map points. Detectors fail on small household objects (mug, bowl) because of sensor noise and limited resolution, so the whole pipeline fails.
motivation: Small daily household objects matter for service robots, yet prior ObjectNav work targets large goals such as chair, couch and bed. Humans use context to find small objects (a mug is likely on a cabinet or table), so a learned mapper could infer likely object locations from surrounding large objects even when the detector misses the goal.
key_idea: Replace detector-based semantic mapping with a learned probabilistic semantic map whose mapper takes RGBD plus a latent context vector from the current map, and use it to guide exploration toward likely object locations.
insight: The learned mapper can predict small objects from contextual cues (e.g. a mug on a cabinet) when the detector fails, shown qualitatively in Fig. 4. Quantitatively, on small-object goals success rises from 0.43 to 0.69 and SPL from 0.186 to 0.382 over Neural SLAM. On big objects the two are nearly equal (0.72 vs 0.73), so the gain comes from context and probabilistic mapping for small objects. No ablations of the individual components (normalized BCE, priority sampling, context encoder) are reported.
method: Probabilistic semantic map: a C×N×N global map updated in logit space, L(e|o_T,o_1:T-1)=L(e|o_T)+L(e|o_1:T-1)-L(e), i.e. approximate Bayesian fusion of per-step egocentric predictions via differentiable spatial transforms
Probabilistic mapping module: visual encoder (first 8 layers of pretrained ResNet50 for RGB plus a trained CNN for depth, concatenated) predicts an egocentric C×M×M map (5cm cells)
Context encoder: crops a 128×128 local map centred on the agent and encodes it with a CNN into a latent context vector z, fused with visual features by an MLP and decoded by transposed convs
Normalized BCE loss: the per-class loss is normalized by the class's object size in the local map, with β penalizing false positives, so small objects are not overshadowed by large ones

Priority sampling: discretizes (x,y,θ) configurations, stores BCE loss per grid in a replay buffer, and samples configurations with probability proportional to loss·γ^N, so training focuses on past errors

Navigation: Neural SLAM predicts an obstacle map; frontier-based exploration is used while the probabilistic map is empty; the high-level goal is chosen from the probabilistic map; the low-level action comes from a goal distance map on the obstacle map

setting.backbone: ResNet50 (first 8 layers, pretrained) + depth CNN + context CNN + MLP + transposed-conv decoder (trained); Neural SLAM for obstacle mapping; FBE exploration
setting.training_data: 8000 generated episodes over 8 house layouts, iGibson scenes augmented with randomly placed household objects (books, bowls, mugs, etc.) on commonsense receptacles
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MOVE FORWARD, TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT, STOP
setting.privileged: GT semantic map used only for training supervision; none at test time

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 test episodes on 2 novel house layouts
numbers.backbone: probabilistic mapper (ResNet50+depth CNN+context encoder) with FBE
numbers.extra: trained on 8000 generated episodes; small goals: mug, bowl, snack box, book, frypan, earphone

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 test episodes on 2 novel house layouts
numbers.backbone: probabilistic mapper (ResNet50+depth CNN+context encoder) with FBE
numbers.extra: big object goals such as chair, couch, plant, bed, toilet, TV

numbers_note: Success is printed as fractions (0.69) in Table 1, so SR is recorded as printed rather than as a percentage. The split name 'test' is used because the 200 episodes come from held-out layouts. Only Table 1 has results, and there are no ablations.
results: On small-object goals, the method reaches Success 0.69, SPL 0.382 and DTS 0.294, versus 0.43 / 0.186 / 1.957 for the Neural SLAM + FBE baseline (about +26 points success, +105% SPL). On big-object goals it is roughly on par (0.73 vs 0.72 success).
limitations: Evaluated only on a small custom simulated benchmark (200 test episodes, 2 layouts) with synthetically placed objects; no standard benchmark or real robot
Only compared against one baseline (Neural SLAM + FBE) and uses a hand-designed frontier exploration policy rather than a learned one; no ablations of the proposed components
Placement of objects follows commonsense receptacle rules, so context gains may partly reflect the synthetic data generation bias
builds_on: Neural SLAM / Goal-Oriented Semantic Exploration (Chaplot et al.)
